title: Half-window PPG respiratory-rate drift fails to improve breath-interval variability prediction in two public cohorts
abstract: Adding normalized half-window PPG respiratory-rate drift worsened prediction of log1p interbreath-interval CV: equal-record MSE gain was -0.00009177 in BIDMC (95% record-bootstrap CI -0.00018057, -0.00001982) and -0.00005661 in independent CapnoBase (-0.00008049, -0.00003516). This fixed drift feature did not add useful physiological variability information to the tested spectral-summary model. A prespecified ridge regression comparison used 53 ICU records for grouped cross-validation and frozen model fitting, then 42 perioperative records for external transport. The target was annotated breathing variability, not disease or ventilator outcome. Negative results survived robust-reference and in-band checks. Both datasets were previously analyzed by this worker, so external testing is not untouched confirmation.
